messages:
julia: Heads-up — noticed a confusing gap: tenant quota throttles show up in console but the SLO alert (error budget) didn't fire, so oncall didn't realize tenants were impacted. Can we surface a single 'effective threshold' that explains when an alert will actually route?

anil: Short summary: quota vs SLO are computed on different signals. Quota is instantaneous QPS limits, SLO alerts evaluate error budget over windows. They don't map 1:1 — we should expose a derived value that the console can show. :thinking_face: 

kate_pm: UX ask: show the computed value inline with tooltip "why this would alert" + link to raw signals. Also need rollout plan: internal tenants only -> 10% pilot -> all. Keep toggleable.

mike_sre: Prefer server-side computation and emit it as a metric so all consumers (console, paging) read the same number. Frontend computation leads to drift and pager confusion.

anil: Tradeoffs noted. Implementation idea: evaluate effective threshold when we run SLO evaluation job and emit a short-lived timeseries metric `derived_alert_threshold.{tenant}.{slo}`. Console reads that instead of recalculating. That avoids expensive joins in UI.

julia: Quick sketch of the payload we'd store / surface:
```json
{
  "tenant": "acme-corp",
  "slo_id": "p95_latency_ms",
  "slo_window": "30d",
  "slo_threshold": "500",
  "quota_qps": "1200",
  "recent_throttle_count": "24",
  "effective_threshold": "480",
  "reason": "throttle_headroom + error_budget_shortfall"
}
```

anil: Exactly. Then console UI shows `effective_threshold` and an expandable "why" list that includes recent throttle spikes, error budget burn rate, and routing fallbacks.

mike_sre: One more: noise control. If we surface this derived threshold, we'll risk duplicate signals — page SLO leads + tenant owner. Suggest we treat derived alerts as annotations and route them to lower priority channel or tenant-specific channel unless they trip canonical SLO rule. For example: annotate with `derived=true` and add a suppression window: if `throttle_count > 0` then suppress global page for 5m and send tenant-notice.

kate_pm: That sounds good. We should also show simulated impact in console before enabling for a tenant: a 'preview' that runs the derived calc on last 30d and highlights differences.

anil: Implementation to-dos (short):
- add `derived_alert_threshold` metric in evaluation job
- console: new column + details panel + preview mode
- paging: annotate derived alerts and update routing rules
- rollout: feature flag + per-tenant opt-in

mike_sre: Add oncall test plan: enable on staging tenants, run synthetic throttle generator, verify only tenant notice fires + one global test alert.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: `feature/alerting/effective-threshold` -> staging (preview link: https://ci.internal.redwood/deploy/9876) :rocket:

julia: Thanks — I'll write the RFC with mockups and include the preview flow. Can folks review by EOD Wednesday? :eyes:

anil: Reviewing after lunch. I can prototype the eval metric this week.

kate_pm: I'll draft rollout checklist and owner list.

mike_sre: I'll add the oncall tests to the runbook.

julia: Cool — next sync if we hit blockers. :thumbsup:
